articles.title: Dor durante a relação? Entenda quando o corpo alerta para algo errado | G1
articles.standfirst: Frequentemente, a dor está ligada a focos de endometriose instalados atrás do útero.
articles.summary: Frequentemente, a dor está ligada a focos de endometriose instalados atrás do útero.
articles.body:
É uma cena que se repete no escuro do quarto, sem que ninguém saiba: no meio de um momento que deveria ser de entrega, o corpo trava, vem um aperto por dentro, e ela finge que está tudo bem para não interromper o momento. Depois, inventa uma desculpa para a próxima vez, cansaço, estresse, qualquer coisa para não passar por isso de novo.

Esse tipo de dor durante a relação tem nome na medicina: dispareunia. Entre 10% e 28% das mulheres sentem esse sintoma em algum momento da vida, por diferentes causas. Já entre as que passam por cirurgia com diagnóstico confirmado de endometriose, esse número sobe para cerca de 45%.

Por que a endometriose causa esse tipo de dor

A endometriose acontece quando um tecido parecido com o que reveste o útero por dentro cresce em lugares onde não devia estar. Quando esses focos se instalam atrás do útero, provocam inflamação e fazem os tecidos ao redor colarem uns nos outros. Durante a relação sexual, as estruturas da pelve se movem naturalmente, e se há lesões bem nessa região, esse movimento traciona um tecido já inflamado. É isso que gera a dor profunda, muitas vezes sentida mais ao fundo, e não na entrada do corpo.

O peso emocional de uma dor que ninguém vê

Além do desconforto físico, existe outro lado dessa dor que raramente é discutido: o medo e o silêncio. Muitas vezes o próprio parceiro não entende o que está acontecendo, o que afasta ainda mais o casal do assunto e adia a busca por tratamento, inclusive o cirúrgico quando ele é necessário. "Por vergonha, ou por acreditar que o problema é ‘da cabeça’, muitas mulheres demoram anos para contar isso ao médico, o que também atrasa o diagnóstico" , explica Tiago Castilho, cirurgião oncológico com atuação em cirurgia ginecológica e cirurgia de endometriose profunda.

Nem toda dor na relação é sinal de doença grave, mas um padrão que se repete, especialmente quando a dor é profunda e vem acompanhada de cólica fora do período menstrual ou dor para evacuar, merece investigação. O diagnóstico depende de uma avaliação ginecológica cuidadosa, muitas vezes complementada por exames de imagem específicos, como o ultrassom transvaginal com preparo intestinal e a ressonância magnética da pelve.

Para entender melhor os efeitos dessa dor na vida do casal, veja o artigo completo sobre dor durante a relação sexual e dispareunia na endometriose.

Dor durante a relação não é algo que a mulher deva simplesmente aprender a suportar. Existem diferentes causas possíveis, e a endometriose é uma delas.

Há mais de 10 anos, Tiago Castilho acompanha e opera mulheres com endometriose, incluindo casos de doença profunda. Sua atuação combina técnicas minimamente invasivas, como videocirurgia e cirurgia robótica, e, quando há indicação cirúrgica, o Cuidado 360º amplia o cuidado para os aspectos físicos e emocionais da preparação e da recuperação.

Para mais informações ou agendamento de consulta, entre em contato pelo telefone (44) 99169-8161.

Tiago Castilho é Cirurgião Oncológico com atuação em Cirurgia Ginecológica e Cirurgia de Endometriose Profunda, mestre e doutor na área, com mais de 10 anos de experiência no tratamento cirúrgico da doença. CRM-PR 22590 | RQE 2911 | RQE 844.

articles.title: TRE-PB retoma atendimento ao eleitor para tirar dúvidas de votação | G1
articles.standfirst: O canal direto atende eleitores com dúvidas sobre o processo de votação. O serviço funciona das 8h às 18h em dias úteis e das 8h às 19h nos finais de semana.
articles.summary: O Serviço de Atendimento ao Eleitor do TRE-PB funciona por telefone e WhatsApp para esclarecer dúvidas sobre local de votação, documentos e justificativa.
articles.body:
TRE-PB retoma Serviço de Atendimento ao Eleitor nesta sexta-feira (16) — Foto: ROBERTO CASIMIRO/FOTOARENA/ESTADÃO CONTEÚDO

A Justiça Eleitoral da Paraíba retoma nesta sexta-feira (16) o atendimento online para esclarecer dúvidas dos eleitores sobre a votação. O serviço funciona das 8h às 18h nos dias úteis e das 8h às 19h aos sábados e domingos.

O atendimento do Serviço de Atendimento ao Eleitor (SAE) ocorre por meio de ligação ou WhatsApp pelo telefone oficial (83) 3512-1500.

Segundo o Tribunal Regional Eleitoral da Paraíba (TRE-PB), os eleitores podem consultar a situação eleitoral, confirmar o local de votação, saber quais documentos levar, obter orientações sobre como justificar a ausência e verificar se têm biometria cadastrada.

No segundo turno, marcado para 25 de outubro, o atendimento começa às 6h e segue até o encerramento da votação, previsto para as 17h.

Entre 24 de setembro e 6 de outubro, o Serviço de Atendimento ao Eleitor (SAE) realizou 2.740 atendimentos. Desse total, 1.856 foram feitos pelo chat e 882 por telefone.

As principais dúvidas foram sobre documentos de identificação, voto em trânsito, local e seção de votação, justificativa eleitoral, multas e situação do título de eleitor. Também houve perguntas sobre treinamento e convocação de mesários.

articles.title: Veja íntegra da entrevista com Allyson (União) no Inter 1 | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato foi o entrevistado desta sexta-feira (16) do Inter 1. Cadu de Lula (PT), que também disputa o 2º turno, foi entrevistado na quinta (15).
articles.summary: Candidato foi o entrevistado desta sexta-feira (16) do Inter 1. Cadu de Lula (PT), que também disputa o 2º turno, foi entrevistado na quinta (15).
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte Allyson Bezerra ( União Brasil ), entrevistado desta sexta-feira (16) do Inter 1 , disse que vai reduzir a fila de cirurgias eletivas no estado pela metade em até seis meses e também prometeu a construção da terceira ponte para a Zona Norte de Natal .

Segundo o candidato, reduzir a fila de cirurgias será possível através da contratação de profissionais que vão atuar junto com os servidores.

"Nos primeiros 6 meses de gestão, metade dessa fila nós vamos zerar. E vamos fazer isso com contratação direta de equipes de profissionais que vão trabalhar junto com os nossos servidores nos hospitais regionais do estado", falou.

Allyson Bezerra (União) entrevistado do Inter 1 — Foto: Fernanda Zauli/g1

O Inter 1 entrevistou, nesta semana, os dois candidatos ao governo do Rio Grande do Norte que disputam o segundo turno, que tem votação prevista para o dia 25 de outubro.

Nesta quinta-feira (15), o entrevistado foi Cadu de Lula ( PT ). Na sexta (16), o entrevistado foi o candidato Allyson Bezerra (União Brasil).

Desburocratizar o Estado e relação com presidente eleito

O candidato iniciou a entrevista criticando as dívidas do estado e disse que pretende "desburocratizar" o estado para o recebimento de empresários e novos empreendimentos.

"É uma trava tão grande que se um empreendedor, se um cidadão for buscar o Idema para regularizar o empreendimento, ele vai perder anos tentando e não vai conseguir. Nós precisamos desburocratizar o Estado. Para isso eu trago a liberdade econômica", disse.

Allyson disse estar "convencido" de que o processo de desburocratização vai aumentar o nível de arrecadação do estado, o que, caso seja eleito, iria colaborar para realizar os investimentos previstos no plano de governo.

"Nós vamos viabilizar através de emendas parlamentares, vamos viabilizar através do Governo Federal com parceria, vamos viabilizar o aumento da arrecadação vindo justamente de novos empreendimentos que vamos ter no governo do Estado, que irá trabalhar para viabilizar. Nós seremos parceiros daqueles que querem empreender no Rio Grande do Norte"

Na entrevista, o candidato falou ainda sobre não ter declarado apoio a nenhum dos dois candidatos à presidência da República que disputam o segundo turno - Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Segundo Allyson, caso seja eleito, ele será capaz de dialogar com qualquer um que seja eleito.

"Eu tenho a capacidade, sou o único candidato que tem a capacidade de conversar em Brasília, seja qual for o presidente da República que seja eleito. Nós temos a condição de levar os projetos que são prioritários para Brasília e para a bancada federal. Não terei dificuldade de conversar com nenhum dos três senadores e dos oito deputados eleitos federais do Rio Grande do Norte", falou.

Ele citou o período em que foi prefeito em Mossoró - por quase dois mandatos -, período em que o país foi governado tanto por Jair Bolsonaro (PL) como por Lula (PT), rivais políticos.

"Nós temos pessoas que pensam diferente. Por isso que temos que ter um governante que tenha a capacidade de sentar na mesa e dialogar", falou.

O candidato também falou sobre a construção da terceira ponte, que consta no plano de governo. Segundo ele, o projeto é previsto para ter acesso da Avenida Itapetinga, na Zona Norte de Natal, até a Zona Leste - o segundo ponto não foi detalhado.

Ele citou ainda a experiência em obras de infraestrutura enquanto prefeito de Mossoró, como pontes e rodovias.

"A gente precisa ter um projeto detalhado, com um traçado. O traçado é da Avenida Itapetinga, da Zona Norte de Natal, ligando com a Zona Leste. Então, nós queremos fazer essa grande obra e vamos fazer", disse.

Allyson falou que, caso eleito, vai realizar a contratação de técnicos para iniciar o planejamento da obra já no início do mandato e, em seguida, buscar os recursos através de parceria com o governo federal.

"Nós vamos fazer uma contratação de técnicos que vão trabalhar para fazer o planejamento do estudo geológico, do estudo do traçado, do estudo do trânsito, do estudo das externalidades da obra para que a gente consiga definir o orçamento e, aí, sim, buscar a bancada federal, buscar o Ministério da Infraestrutura", falou.

O candidato falou ainda sobre parcerias com a iniciativa privada para outras obras. Ele citou, entre os exemplos, a construção de um estádio em Mossoró, onde foi prefeito.

"Um investimento de mais de R$ 215 milhões, que a prefeitura não vai desembolsar nenhum real, porque a iniciativa privada está construindo o estádio e vai construir também um centro administrativo", falou.

Relação com os servidores e reduzir filas de cirurgias

Questionado sobre cobranças que recebeu de servidores municipais durante o mandato enquanto prefeito de Mossoró, Allyson disse que vai ter "relacionamento direto" com o servidor estadual, caso seja eleito.

Ele citou ainda a experiência de ser um servidor concursado da Universidade Federal Rural do Semi-Árido (Ufersa).

"Quando eu assumi também a gestão [em Mossoró], eu vi o comprometimento com o pessoal. Nós estamos garantindo direitos, buscamos trabalhar com desenvolvimento para a receita aumentar", disse.

Sobre a fila de cirurgias eletivas no estado, o candidato disse que vai reduzi-la na metade em até seis meses. Ele disse que haverá um trabalho para regionalizar a saúde no estado.

"Essa regionalização da saúde é porque eu conheci. Eu sou um candidato que conhece o Rio Grande do Norte por inteiro. Eu conheço porque eu estou desde março estudando detalhadamente cada cidade, cada região, cada hospital", completou.

O candidato disse ainda que tem como meta aumentar a nota do Rio Grande do Norte no Ideb de 4 para 6,1. O Índice de Desenvolvimento da Educação Básica (Ideb) avalia o nível da educação estadual e nacional.

"Aí alguém diz: 'Allyson, isso é impossível no Rio Grande do Norte porque o Rio Grande do Norte está com nota 3, com nota 4'. Bem, eu te dou a nota que eu já fiz como prefeito", disse.

Allyson disse ainda que vai dar um incentivo financeiro a estudantes em vulnerabilidade social que passem de ano.

"Nós vamos colocar isso para que todo o jovem do Rio Grande do Norte que tenha vulnerabilidade social, ele receba essa bolsa. Ao final do ano escolar, ele passando de ano, vai receber R$ 1 mil no PIX", falou.

Nas considerações finais, o candidato criticou o candidato adversário e o atual governo, reforçou os projetos que constam no plano de governo, como a terceira ponte e o programa para atrair empreendedores ao estado, e pediu votos pela mudança.

"Então eu estou muito seguro de dizer aqui a você, potiguar, a você, minha amiga, a você, meu amigo, a você, jovem, e principalmente, a você, mulher, quem mais está sofrendo no Rio Grande do Norte, eu acredito que são as mulheres. Sofrendo, a mãe está sofrendo com a insegurança quando o seu filho sai de casa. A mãe está sofrendo com o sangramento, uma mulher sofrendo com o sangramento, o precisando de uma cirurgia ou vendo o seu esposo, o seu filho precisando de uma cirurgia que não tem", disse.

"E está sofrendo porque infelizmente está vendo as nossas escolas estaduais danificadas, sem ter futuro, sem ter melhora. Eu quero conversar com cada um de vocês e dizer, vamos mudar. Não podemos mais ficar nesse estado que está do mesmo jeito que começou há 8 anos. Nós queremos mudança", afirmou.

articles.title: Greve de ônibus em Macapá: Nova Macapá paralisa frota pela 3ª vez | G1
articles.standfirst: Passageiros enfrentaram transtornos na manhã desta sexta-feira (16). A empresa Nova Macapá alega atrasos no pagamento de salários e do vale-alimentação. Em nota, a prefeitura informou que os repasses à empresa estão em dia.
articles.summary: Greve de ônibus em Macapá afeta passageiros nesta sexta-feira (16) devido a atrasos no vale-alimentação, enquanto a prefeitura afirma que repasses estão em dia.
articles.body:
Rodoviários da empresa Nova Macapá estão de greve — Foto: Reprodução

Pela terceira vez em menos de dois meses, funcionários da empresa Nova Macapá , responsável por grande parte do transporte público da capital, entraram em greve. Durante a manhã desta sexta-feira (16), apenas 13 dos 47 ônibus da frota estavam em circulação, e os passageiros enfrentaram dificuldades para se deslocar.

O Sindicato dos Rodoviários denuncia atrasos no pagamento dos salários e do vale-alimentação. Outras duas paralisações já haviam sido realizadas.

A primeira ocorreu em 10 de setembro e durou pouco mais de 24 horas. A segunda foi registrada em 8 de outubro, quando um acordo foi firmado com prazo de cumprimento até o dia 14 deste mês. Segundo o sindicato, porém, o compromisso não foi cumprido.

A entidade que representa os trabalhadores afirma que o vale-alimentação, no valor de pouco mais de R$ 700, continua atrasado. Já os salários foram regularizados apenas na quinta-feira (15).

Parte dos trabalhadores em greve esteve reunida na manhã desta sexta-feira em frente à sede da empresa Nova Macapá , em protesto. De acordo com o sindicato, pelo menos 50 motoristas aderiram à paralisação. Algumas localidades mais afastadas ficaram sem atendimento.

Usuários do transporte público relataram espera superior a uma hora nos pontos de ônibus. O sindicato informou que ainda não há previsão para o encerramento da greve.

"Ontem [quinta-feira] entramos em greve em razão do descumprimento do acordo firmado com a empresa. Ela tinha que pagar os trabalhadores do RH, da manutenção, o vale-alimentação e o retroativo do benefício referente ao mês de junho, mas isso não foi feito", lamentou Max Delis, presidente do sindicato.

Além disso, Delis afirma que trabalhadores saem de férias e não recebem os salários. Em outros casos, funcionários que saíram da empresa há meses ainda não receberam suas rescisões contratuais.

Em nota, a Prefeitura de Macapá , por meio da Companhia de Trânsito e Transporte de Macapá (CTMac), informou que os repasses à empresa Nova Macapá estão rigorosamente em dia, incluindo os valores destinados ao pagamento dos trabalhadores. A administração municipal ressaltou que a quitação dos salários é de responsabilidade exclusiva da empresa.

A CTMac informou ainda que adotará as medidas judiciais cabíveis diante do descumprimento das obrigações por parte da empresa (veja a nota na íntegra ao final desta matéria).

Duas empresas operam o transporte coletivo em Macapá . A Expresso Macapá funciona normalmente. Contudo, segundo o sindicato, a companhia conta com apenas 27 ônibus em operação nas linhas regulares. Já a Nova Macapá é responsável pela maior parcela da frota.

"Queria pedir desculpas à população, pois hoje estão circulando apenas 13 ônibus. Esse número é insuficiente para atender toda a Zona Norte", disse Max.

Segundo o sindicato, a empresa ainda não convocou os trabalhadores para uma nova reunião.

articles.title: Homem que levava 37 cobras venenosas em mala é preso em aeroporto  | G1
articles.standfirst: Cobras, incluindo cascavéis, e lagartos estavam dentro de embalagens de cosméticos guardadas numa mala. Homem afirmou que trazia os animais a pedido de um conhecido brasileiro.
articles.summary: Cobras venenosas e lagartos foram achados em frascos de xampu na bagagem de um mexicano que alegou transportar os animais para um conhecido brasileiro.
articles.body:
Mexicano leva mais de 90 lagartos e cobras venenosas escondidos em bagagem — Foto: Imago/Nature Picture Library

Agentes da alfândega no aeroporto de Colônia/Bonn, no oeste da Alemanha, encontraram mais de 90 lagartos e cobras venenosas escondidos em frascos de cosméticos e meias na bagagem de um viajante mexicano, informaram as autoridades alemãs nesta quinta-feira (16).

O homem, de 45 anos, foi abordado no mês passado e submetido a um exame toxicológico após apresentar um comportamento "nervoso", disseram os agentes da alfândega. Os resultados indicaram que o ele – um bombeiro, cuja identidade não foi revelada pelas autoridades – havia consumido cocaína.

Ao revistarem sua mala, os agentes não encontraram entorpecentes, mas sim cerca de 90 répteis escondidos em recipientes de plástico, frascos de xampu e creme, e meias. Ele chegou em Colônia há três semanas, partindo da Cidade do México com uma escala em Istambul.

"Meus colegas no aeroporto estão acostumados a encontrar todo tipo de 'lembrança' de viagem nas malas, mas nunca tínhamos visto 37 cobras venenosas e 55 lagartos vindos do México", disse Jens Ahland, porta-voz da alfândega.

"Nunca tínhamos feito uma apreensão tão grande"

Entre os animais, havia víboras, cascavéis e diversas espécies de lagartos, incluindo iguanas-de-espinhos, salamandras e lagartos-sem-pata. Segundo Ahland, algumas dessas espécies estão ameaçadas de extinção e sob rigorosa proteção.

Segundo o porta-voz, trata-se de animais raros. "Nunca tínhamos feito uma apreensão tão grande de animais vivos aqui. É angustiante ver o que algumas pessoas fazem com os animais por pura ganância e desejo de lucro."

"Nunca tínhamos feito uma apreensão tão grande de animais vivos aqui", disse porta-voz da alfândega no aeroporto Colônia/Bonn — Foto: Bonn.digital/picture alliance

A alfândega acionou imediatamente veterinários da cidade de Colônia, que cuidaram do atendimento adequado aos animais. Ainda assim, cerca de 30 deles morreram após a longa viagem, na qual permaneceram espremidos e sem comida. Os animais sobreviventes foram levados para um serpentário próximo a Braunschweig.

Durante o interrogatório, o homem de 45 anos declarou que pretendia passar férias na Alemanha e que levou os animais para fazer um favor a um conhecido brasileiro. Um inquérito foi aberto contra o mexicano. Como a Polícia Federal alemã negou sua entrada no país, ele foi enviado de volta a Istambul no dia seguinte à sua chegada.

A alfândega suspeita que o caso se trate de contrabando com fins comerciais. "Os animais provavelmente seriam vendidos aqui e, em seguida, mantidos de forma ilegal", disse Ahland. Os compradores pagariam centenas de euros por algumas espécies.

Segundo Ahland, no ano passado, em todo o território alemão, a alfândega apreendeu quase 57 mil animais e plantas protegidos – ou produtos derivados deles – em mais de 1,3 mil ocorrências. Mais de 90% dessas apreensões ocorreram em encomendas postais ou em aeroportos. Os contrabandistas estão sujeitos a pesadas multas ou até mesmo a penas de prisão.

articles.title: Justiça torna réu motorista acusado de matar ciclista em ciclofaixa  | G1
articles.standfirst: Raphael Costa de Carvalho teve a prisão preventiva decretada após denúncia por homicídio qualificado, omissão de socorro e fuga do local. Vítima estava a caminho do trabalho em São Vicente (SP).
articles.summary: Raphael Costa de Carvalho teve a prisão preventiva decretada após denúncia por homicídio qualificado, omissão de socorro e fuga do local. Vítima estava a caminho do trabalho em São
articles.body:
A Justiça tornou réu o motorista Raphael Costa de Carvalho , acusado de atropelar e matar o ciclista André Luis Menezes da Silva em uma ciclofaixa de São Vicente , no litoral de São Paulo. Ele também teve a prisão preventiva decretada, mas segue foragido .

André era coletor de lixo e estava a caminho do trabalho quando foi atropelado em uma ciclofaixa no bairro Itararé, em 3 de setembro. Com o impacto , ele foi arremessado contra a fachada de um prédio e morreu no local. Raphael fugiu e abandonou o carro poucos quilômetros depois.

Uma garrafa de uísque aberta e um documento de identidade de Raphael foram encontrados no veículo, motivando o pedido de prisão temporária. Conforme apurado pelo g1 , o homem já havia sido preso por embriaguez ao volante e resistência em 2024 .

Em outubro, o Ministério Público de São Paulo (MP-SP) ofereceu denúncia contra Raphael por homicídio qualificado, omissão de socorro e fuga do local, solicitando ainda a decretação da prisão temporária.

Raphael Costa de Carvalho já havia sido preso em flagrante por embriaguez ao volante e resistência, em 2024 — Foto: Diego Bertozzi/TV Tribuna e Reprodução

No documento, o órgão informou que o motorista estava embriagado e dirigindo a cerca de 90,42 km/h em via de velocidade máxima de 40 km/h.

O juiz Alexandre Torres de Aguiar, da 1ª Vara Criminal de São Vicente, recebeu a denúncia, decretou a prisão preventiva e tornou o acusado réu no processo.

“Como bem ponderou a representante do Ministério Público, o crime a ele imputado é hediondo. A forma como foi praticado, bem como seus motivos, denotam ser ele pessoa de índole perigosa”, argumentou o magistrado.

O advogado Ricardo Capusso, que representa o réu, informou que a defesa soube da decisão da Justiça. “Já existe Habeas Corpus impetrado junto ao Tribunal de Justiça, com pedido de contraordem do mandado de prisão”, afirmou.

Ciclista morre após ser atropelado por carro de luxo que invadiu ciclofaixa no litoral de SP — Foto: Reprodução

O passageiro que estava com Raphael no momento do acidente fugiu após abandonar o carro em outra rua também foi denunciado por omissão de socorro.

Posteriormente, ele se apresentou na delegacia e prestou depoimento, dizendo que estava em uma festa com o motorista momentos antes. Para ele, não foi solicitada a prisão, mas o Ministério Público propôs prestação de serviços à comunidade e pagamento de multa.

André Luis Menezes da Silva completaria 46 anos no dia 15 de setembro. Ele era coletor de lixo e morava no bairro Parque Bitaru, mas estava a caminho do trabalho.

André deixou uma filha de um ano do atual relacionamento e um filho adolescente do primeiro casamento.

articles.title: Former Dallas officer Amber Guyger leaves prison on parole after serving 7 years in killing of Botham Jean
articles.summary: Guyger, 38, shot Botham Jean, 26, in 2018 as he sat on his couch eating ice cream. Guyger testified in her criminal trial that she mistook Jean's apartment f...
articles.body:
Former Dallas police Officer Amber Guyger walked free from prison Friday morning after serving seven years behind bars for the murder of Botham Jean.

Guyger, 38, shot 26-year-old Jean inside his apartment in September 2018. He had been sitting on his couch eating ice cream when Guyger, who was off-duty but still in uniform, opened the door. She said she mistook Jean's apartment for her own and believed he was a burglar. He lived on the fourth floor; she lived on the third.

She was found guilty of murder and sentenced to 10 years in prison, but was granted parole earlier this month. Guyger was released after 10 a.m. from the Christina Melton Crain Unit in Gatesville. CBS reported live from the unit, but news cameras didn't capture her release.

Texas Department of Criminal Justice officials said Guyger was released into community supervision.

Guyger was required to travel directly to her new residence and check in immediately with her parole officer, according to Texas parole requirements .

She was allowed to take home personal items accumulated while in prison and will either wear state-issued civilian clothes or clothes brought to her by visitors or the people picking her up. Guyger walked out with her parole papers, a temporary ID and a prepaid debit card or check for money left in her inmate trust account.

Guyger was denied parole in 2024 after the state parole board said she was not rehabilitated or ready for release.

Her request was granted this time after a review found her record showed no documented pattern of violence, that she maintained a "satisfactory institutional adjustment" and that she completed a treatment plan that "should enhance" her chances of obtaining — and keeping — a full-time job, a Texas Board of Pardons and Paroles spokesperson said in early October.

The board has several options for what type of parole to grant an inmate, a vote that depends on individual circumstances and the inmate's behavior during time served.

Guyger was granted direct release with no additional restrictions beyond her parole conditions, the least restrictive form of parole approval a Texas inmate can receive.

The decision to release her sparked a new wave of interest and emotion around the case, which drew international attention, sparked protests and led Texas lawmakers to pass the Botham Jean Act.

Also known as Bo's Law, the statute requires officers to keep their body cameras on for the entirety of their participation in an investigation. That same year, Dallas renamed part of South Lamar Street for Jean.

"The past eight years have been an incredibly traumatic and painful experience for Botham Jean's family," the family said in an official statement released in early October. "The loss of Botham has left our family forever dismembered, and that is something we continue to live with every day."

Guyger's parole conditions were not released, but her trial attorney, who no longer represents her, told The Dallas Morning News after the parole vote that she has a job that will keep her out of the public life and a living arrangement that will stay private.

"She's hopeful, optimistic, tremendously remorseful," attorney Robert Rogers said. "That's probably something she'll always live with."

Most parolees must follow the same basic set of rules, alongside any special conditions decided by the parole board, which are typically kept confidential.

Guyger will have to follow her parole conditions until September 2029.

Failure to follow the conditions can result in parole revocation, which sends the inmate back to prison for the remainder of their sentence, or lesser sanctions such as curfew adjustments or brief incarceration in a facility designed for parolees.

State law requires all parolees to get permission from their parole officer if they want to change residences or leave the state. They must be working or in school, and they have to check in regularly with their parole officer, submit monthly education or work reports, and submit to random alcohol and drug testing and unannounced searches.

They're forbidden from breaking the law, owning or being around firearms and ammunition, and from contacting the victim directly or indirectly. They must make restitution payments and reimburse the prison for some educational programs.

Guyger still faces a judgment of nearly $100 million from a federal civil suit connected to Jean's murder.

A large photo of Botham Jean is displayed with photos and cards on one of the tables in his childhood home in Castries, St. Lucia on Sept. 25, 2018. Botham Jean was shot and killed in his apartment by off-duty Dallas police Officer Amber Guyger. (Vernon Bryant/Staff Photographer)

articles.title: An Iowa couple bought 40 acres choked with invasive plants; after discovering rare ecosystems beneath the overgrowth, they restored the land into wetlands attracting sandhill cranes
articles.summary: What appeared to be a neglected field in Madison County, Iowa, concealed remnants of rare native ecosystems.
articles.body: What appeared to be a neglected field in Madison County, Iowa, concealed remnants of rare native ecosystems. When John and Sheri Paule bought the first 40 acres of their property, its hillsides were overrun with invasive vegetation, leaving little indication of what the landscape might once have been. Surviving bur oak trees, however, offered a clue that the land could have supported an oak savanna. A subsequent visit by an ecologist revealed remnants of a sedge meadow, wet meadow and a transition zone between habitats. The discovery reshaped the couple's conservation efforts. Working with the US Department of Agriculture's Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) and other specialists, they began restoring wetlands and protecting native habitats across a landscape spanning more than 300 acres.How an Iowa couple discovered rare ecosystems beneath invasive plantsWhen the Paules first assessed their property from the road, the land had little visual appeal. John Paule recalled that the hillsides were choked with multiflora rose, prickly ash and other invasive vegetation. The surviving bur oaks, however, suggested that an oak savanna might once have existed there.The ecological significance became clearer when Tom Rosburg, a biology professor at Drake University, visited the site. He identified remnants of a sedge meadow, wet meadow and a transition zone between habitats. These native ecosystems have become increasingly rare in Iowa, making their protection an important part of the restoration project.The discovery shifted the focus from clearing overgrowth to recovering the landscape's ecological character. Rather than treating the property as simply an overgrown field, the Paules worked with conservation specialists to protect what remained and improve conditions for native plants and wildlife.How the couple began restoring the wetlandsThe restoration involved more than removing invasive plants. The Paules worked with NRCS and its conservation partners to improve wetland function, manage vegetation and develop a long-term plan for the property.An existing wetland easement had been enrolled in the Emergency Wetland Reserve Program in 1998. In 2023, the Iowa NRCS Easement Team worked with civil engineer Nick Campbell to design a meandering wetland restoration using stewardship funding under the Agricultural Conservation Easement Program's Wetland Reserve Easements initiative.The specific wetland restoration covered approximately 70 acres. Restoration measures included native seeding and brush management, with the aim of improving habitat for wildlife such as sandhill cranes.NRCS provided technical guidance and helped develop a conservation plan to guide continued management. According to the agency, stewardship funding covered 100% of the construction, seeding and management costs incurred through this restoration process. This funding arrangement relates to the eligible costs of the project, not necessarily every expense associated with owning and managing the property.Sandhill cranes and hundreds of blue-winged teal use the restored landscapeThe restoration's effects are visible in the wildlife using the property. Paule told NRCS that sandhill cranes use the restored wetlands, while red-headed woodpeckers regularly appear in the oak savanna.He also recalled an unusual sighting of hundreds of blue-winged teal remaining on the property for two or three weeks. He said the couple had not experienced such an occurrence before.These observations suggest that the restored habitats are being used by a variety of birds. However, the available account does not provide a formal before-and-after wildlife census, so the sightings should not be treated as evidence of a quantified increase in bird populations.The wetlands also retain water where it previously moved quickly through the landscape, while native vegetation continues to expand. Researchers, university classes and conservation professionals have visited the property to learn about its ecosystems and restoration work.The Paules' project addresses a wider conservation challenge in Iowa, where extensive drainage and development have dramatically reduced the state's original wetlands. According to the Iowa Department of Natural Resources, wetlands once covered approximately 4 million to 6 million acres of the state, and nearly 95% have been drained.Healthy wetlands can store floodwater, improve water quality, support groundwater recharge under suitable conditions and provide habitat for wildlife. Sedge meadows and wet meadows also support specialised plant communities that can be lost when water patterns change or invasive vegetation dominates.By improving wetland function and protecting native habitat remnants, the Paules are helping conserve ecological features that have become increasingly uncommon in the state. Their work also demonstrates how private landowners can collaborate with public conservation agencies and specialists to restore damaged landscapes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 'Snakebite' murder: UP court cites Manusmriti verse while pronouncing death sentence
articles.summary: MEERUT: A local court in Meerut on Friday sentenced a woman and her lover to death for murdering her husband and attempting to pass it off as a snakebite
articles.body: MEERUT: A local court in Meerut on Friday sentenced a woman and her lover to death for murdering her husband and attempting to pass it off as a snakebite death, citing the Manusmriti and its assertion that "fear of punishment keeps society under control".The court also invoked the mythological figure Savitri, who bargained with Yama to save her husband's life, observing that a wife is considered her husband's better half, government counsel Farzana Maqsood said.Additional district and sessions judge Jaiveer Singh Nagar opened the 131-page judgment with a verse from the Manusmriti on a ruler's duties and the importance of maintaining order in society.Explaining the original verse, the judgment stated: "Fear of punishment keeps society under control. Without punishment, the wicked would prey upon the righteous."The judgment further said that unrighteousness would never triumph over the righteous, referring to the Manusmriti.The court classified the case as "rarest of rare" and sentenced Ravita and Amardeep to death for murdering Amit Kashyap and destroying evidence. The two were convicted on October 7.The prosecution sought the maximum punishment, citing the gravity and brutality of the crime. Government counsel Farzana Maqsood and the victim's lawyer Balraj Singh presented arguments on behalf of the prosecution, also referring to previous Supreme Court and high court judgments.According to police, Amit was found dead on a cot at his home in Akbarpur Sadat village, in Meerut's Bahsuma area, on April 13, 2025. A live snake was found beside his body, prompting his family to initially suspect a snakebite.However, the postmortem revealed injury marks on his neck and nose, suggesting that he had died by strangulation, police said.Amit's brother, Monu, filed an FIR against Ravita and Amardeep on April 16, 2025.The prosecution said Ravita and Amardeep were in a relationship and that Amit had learnt about it, leading to frequent disputes between the couple. The two allegedly strangled him and placed a live snake beside his body to make the murder appear to be a snakebite death.Before the sentencing, Ravita sought leniency, citing her three young children, while Amardeep pointed to his elderly parents.Amit's mother, Munesh Devi, welcomed the verdict, saying the family had sought the death penalty from the beginning and had received justice.The sentence comes two days after another court in Meerut sentenced Muskan Rastogi and her lover Sahil Shukla to death for murdering Muskan's husband, Saurabh Rajput, and concealing his dismembered body in a blue drum.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Meerut | Silver Rate in Meerut | Bank Holidays in Meerut | Public Holidays in Meerut | Meerut AQI | Weather in Meerut | Petrol Price in Meerut | Diesel Price in Meerut | CNG Price in Meerut | LPG Price in MeerutStay updated with the latest Meerut news. articles.title: Son carries on teaching legacy of parents missing in Nepal floods
articles.summary: Mala and Bipin Patel, who run a tuition business in Coventry, were in Nepal during the August floods.
articles.body:
A son whose parents remain missing after the catastrophic floods in Nepal has vowed to continue the family business to "honour their legacy".

Deepesh Patel said he and his brother were "taking it one step at a time" as they await news of their mother Mala and father Bipin, who crossed from Nepal into Tibet before a landslide struck the Gyirong border seven weeks ago.

While the search continues, Patel, from Coventry, has taken on responsibility for his parents' First Class Learning business which provides after-school academic tuition in the city.

"I'm sure my parents would have would have wanted it to carry on, and I'll do my best to try and fill their shoes," Patel said.

"There's a lot of people dependent on it so I'm just kind of taking things step by step," he added.

His parents were travelling on a pilgrimage through Nepal towards Tibet when floods struck on 26 August.

More than 5,300 people remain missing, said the United Nations, after the floods which were triggered by a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border.

Patel worked in sales prior to taking on the family business which runs centres at Caledon Castle School and Walsgrave Baptist Church in Coventry, and he is adapting to running the firm.

"I was in sales before so it's a bit of a switch for sure - dealing with children you have to have a lot of patience," he told BBC CWR.

"I know my mum definitely had a lot of patience, so I try and draw upon that experience to an extent."

Patel said running the business was also helping to keep him focused and giving him a sense of purpose while the family were "still in the dark" about what had happened to his mother, Mala, and father, Bipin.

"As a family we're taking it one step at a time, it is difficult times and we are just getting used to a new reality," Patel said.

"We haven't heard any information since".

Patel said relatives of people unaccounted for had created a group chat to share updates and support one another.

"We have talked to them and we are all in the same boat in that respect. We are just helping each other where we can," he added.

He said the support from friends and family had been invaluable and "means a lot at this point in time".

His brother, Anant, previously told the BBC the family last heard from their parents on 25 August. He also said their father had been a devoted Coventry City supporter for more than 40 years .

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office said: "The scenes along the Nepal-China border are devastating and our thoughts remain with all those affected by this tragedy, and with those still waiting for news of loved ones.

"Supporting British nationals and their families remains our priority, and our staff continue to provide consular support to those affected."

articles.title: SIR protests: Opposition has found common ground. But can it stay united?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: \"All protests are one,\" Congress leader Rahul Gandhi declared on Wednesday as opposition parties rallied behind two Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)
articles.body: NEW DELHI: "All protests are one," Congress leader Rahul Gandhi declared on Wednesday as opposition parties rallied behind two Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders sent to judicial custody following demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke welcomed Rahul's support, thanking the Congress leader for standing with the arrested protesters.Just days ago, that was hardly how things looked on Delhi's streets, where Congress and CJP appeared to be competing for space and prominence while leading separate campaigns against alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Congress-led INDIA bloc was organising its own demonstrations, while CJP, which had mobilised thousands of protesters in July, prepared separately for Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10.AAP, TMC and the Left were willing to join CJP's agitation, but Congress kept its distance. Their objective was the same, but they were fighting for it separately. Many wondered why.On October 10, the Delhi police enforced an unprecedented clampdown in the national capital to prevent mobilisation for CJP’s Jantar Mantar 2.0. Thousands of protesters were dragged on the streets and detained.Such was the intensity of police action that the CJP stir could not even take off. The top CJP leaders were arrested from a plane on landing in Delhi, drawing flak from some quarters for their easy “surrender.” Several political parties stood with the cockroaches, but the Congress stayed away.The trigger for greater unity came after CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were arrested on October 14 following their attempt to protest at Jantar Mantar by waving the Tricolour. Rahul Gandhi came out in open support for first time, and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke thanked him.The dynamics now seem to be changing, with Congress and CJP more willing to support each other, if not formally join forces. But why? Have both sides realised the limitations of organising separate protests for the same cause? Let's decode this shift.From NEET protests to Jantar Mantar 2.0In June, when CJP protested against the NEET paper leak and demanded the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Congress stayed away. Rahul was leading his own programme, Chhatron Ki Goonj, on similar issues.AAP, the Left and social activists joined CJP at Jantar Mantar. The movement gained momentum with Sonam Wangchuk and AISA leader Neha Bora sitting on an indefinite fast. But Congress continued to stay away.On July 20, Delhi Police launched a major operation against students and young protesters who had reached the capital on CJP's call. The next day, Rahul joined the agitation and staged a sit-in outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence, shifting Congress's focus from its own campaign.However, with the government entering negotiations with CJP and later accepting its demands, including Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, Congress was left on the sidelines.The anti-paper leak protests were perhaps a wake-up call for political parties, especially Congress, as large numbers of young people mobilised behind CJP. Prime Minister Modi subsequently turned to Instagram to reach out to Gen Z, while other parties were left to rethink their youth outreach.The SIR and 'vote chori' campaignCongress had been at the forefront of the 'vote chori' campaign, with Rahul holding press conferences highlighting alleged discrepancies in electoral rolls. The party also led a yatra in Bihar ahead assembly elections in the state.The momentum gradually faded, before an Indian Express report on differences within the Election Commission over SIR returned the issue to centre stage. CJP took up the issue, organising a Mumbai rally and setting an October 10 deadline for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, failing which it called for Jantar Mantar 2.0.Congress and the INDIA bloc also stepped up their campaign, announcing a six-point action plan that included an October 6 street protest. With CJP's mobilisation approaching, INDIA bloc leaders returned to the streets for four consecutive days until October 9, perhaps keen not to be left on the sidelines again. But on October 10, the D-day of CJP mobilisation, Rahul was in Chennai and the Congress stayed away.Another change had taken place between July and October. Civil society groups and activists associated with CJP's earlier movement were now actively participating in the INDIA bloc's SIR campaign.The most prominent was Neha Bora, national president of the All India Students' Association (AISA). During the October 12 march towards the Supreme Court, Rahul walked with his hands on the shoulders of Bora and Priyanka Gandhi, with senior opposition leaders following behind.The moment appeared to signal Congress's willingness to bring prominent youth protest faces into its campaign. Political analyst Uday Chandra explained the significance of this shift."Congress under RG recognises that youth-led protests have mobilised ordinary people beyond the reach of traditional party organisations. Neha Bora is an interesting bridge between these worlds, though she leads AISA, a Left student organisation, not CJP," Chandra said.He also pointed to a shift in student politics. "What I find most interesting is that AISA and NSUI are fighting together today. This wasn't the case in the past," he said.As CJP leaders' arrests drew support across party lines, this cooperation was no longer limited to student organisations.Opposition closes ranksThe support for CJP has not come from Congress alone.TMC leader Mamata Banerjee condemned the arrests as an attempt to intimidate young protesters. Party MP Abhishek Banerjee accused the BJP of arresting people for waving the national flag, calling it "BJP's new Pakistanified Bharat". Mahua Moitra also expressed solidarity.AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal questioned whether waving the Tricolour could be a crime. DMK president MK Stalin offered legal assistance to the two CJP leaders, while NCP(SP)'s Supriya Sule and Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Aaditya Thackeray condemned the arrests.The Left maintained its support. Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan criticised the arrests. CPI general secretary D Raja called the police action undemocratic and said his party's student and youth organisations would intensify their campaign for the right to protest at Jantar Mantar.The growing opposition presence was visible beyond Delhi. On Thursday, Vijay's Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), which had stayed away from earlier anti-CEC demonstrations, joined a Congress-led INDIA bloc protest in Chennai. TVK had joined the alliance on October 3; leaders from VCK, MDMK and other partners also participated.More protests may follow. NCP(SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande said Rahul had asked INDIA bloc leaders to be prepared for further demonstrations at 24 hours' notice.These parties have their own priorities and have not always followed the same protest programme. Yet, from Delhi to Chennai, more opposition leaders are speaking out on the same issue. CJP and the INDIA bloc, however, have not announced any joint protest programme.The counterThe BJP has rejected the opposition's allegations, accusing rivals of using street demonstrations to question democratic institutions after electoral defeats.On October 10, BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad said: "We are not opposed to protests, but you have weaponised street protests because of your electoral defeats."BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra also questioned whether events at Jantar Mantar represented the larger picture of India. The Election Commission has denied allegations of political bias in electoral-roll revision.Together, but still separate?For CJP, opposition support presents an opportunity and a challenge. The group has built its identity as an independent youth-led movement, but the detention of its leaders and criticism of its leadership raise questions about sustaining the agitation without established parties.Uday Chandra cautioned against reading too much into the cooperation."There is certainly a convergence of interests at this moment, but we should not mistake that for anything akin to a formal alliance. The police crackdown and detention of protesters have created a common cause for the CJP and the INDIA bloc," Chandra said.He noted that CJP's independence has been central to its youth appeal and that its leaders have criticised the opposition in the past.Political commentator Sugata Srinivasaraju questioned whether CJP had established a support base strong enough to sustain a larger movement. He warned that becoming an extension of Congress could cost it its independent identity. Nor was it clear whether CJP would lead any joint campaign or give way to a larger party.For Congress, CJP's ability to mobilise young people is attractive. But could closer cooperation undermine the independence that made those movements appealing in the first place?Chandra warned: "The autonomy of these youth movements is precisely what makes them politically significant. If parties or their student unions undermine that autonomy, the movement may splinter amidst loud bickering, and can even fizzle out following discord."CJP founder Dipke has maintained that the group will remain an independent pressure group, despite sharing the opposition's demand for Kumar's removal.Has the opposition finally found its feet?The INDIA bloc has struggled to present a united front since its inception. Disagreements over leadership, seat-sharing and political priorities have divided parties, and Congress has faced criticism over its lack of efforts to keep the coalition together.The protests against the CEC have offered a different picture: common ground emerging from demonstrations rather than electoral negotiations. Differences remain, however. AAP and DMK, once part of the INDIA bloc, are still not ready to join hands with Congress.But does a greater presence on the streets mean the opposition has finally found its feet?Sugata Srinivasaraju disagreed that the opposition had been missing in action. Parties, he argued, had always been active, even if street demonstrations had recently become more frequent."More frequent protests do not necessarily mean a more effective opposition. Without planning, structure and a clear strategy, such demonstrations can become counterproductive, with little lasting political impact," he said.He also questioned what the prominence of youth leaders from outside Congress said about its leadership."It also reflects the opposition's inability to lead itself and absence of strong, charismatic leaders of its own. By bringing in faces from youth-led movements, it is, in a way, acknowledging that leadership gap. But there is a risk that leaders like Neha Bora could lose their independent identity within a larger political organisation, much like what happened with Kanhaiya Kumar," he said.The coming together of opposition parties has changed the picture on the streets, but questions remain over whether they can sustain protests, develop new leaders and turn a common cause into a coordinated campaign.For years, the question has been: Where is the opposition? With parties now finding common ground after months of differences, could that question finally have an answer?Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'We'll knock it out fast': Trump says may target Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear facility
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said Washington may strike Iran's Pickaxe mountain facility as he seeks to prevent Tehran from acquiring a nuclear
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Thursday said Washington may strike Iran's Pickaxe mountain facility as he seeks to prevent Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, while ruling out the use of nuclear weapons in the ongoing war.Speaking to Newsmax, Trump said the US was examining the possibility of targeting the site, which is buried deep underground near one of Iran's alleged main nuclear facilities, Reuters reported."Their nuclear is buried under millions of tons of mountain. Now we're looking at Pickaxe Mountain. We may have to go there,” Trump said.“We'll take a shot at that one. We'll knock it out fast," he added.Trump also rejected the need to deploy nuclear weapons against Iran, saying the US could achieve its objectives without them."I wouldn't use nuclear. We don't have to," Trump told the news outlet.Trump said the US wanted to ensure the nuclear weapons never fall into Iranian hands "because if they had it, they would use it."He reiterated that he was not considering sending American ground troops into the country.The war began in February with US-Israeli strikes against Iran.Trump did not clarify whether he had authorised the use of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB), commonly known as the “mother of all bombs”, against Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites.However, he stressed that the MOAB was not a nuclear weapon.According to Anadolu Agency, Iran’s Pickaxe Mountain lies around 1.5 kilometres south of the Natanz nuclear facility and is believed to house nuclear centrifuges relocated from other sites. The mountain is made of solid granite and extends to a depth of up to 600 metres, with Iran allegedly excavating more than 100 metres beneath it.There have also been unverified claims that some of Iran’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium may be stored at the site, where it could be further enriched for potential use in nuclear weapons.Earlier, Iran foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said “no nuclear activity is taking place” at Pickaxe Mountain, dismissing US threats as “a fabricated pretext for aggression, destruction, and sabotage”.You use AI every day. articles.title: Palestinians and US journalist injured by Israeli settlers in West Bank harvest attack
articles.summary: The BBC sees masked settlers attack Palestinians trying to harvest olives, amid a surge in similar incidents.
articles.body:
Dozens of masked settlers have attacked Palestinians and set fire to cars and olive trees during the annual olive harvest in the occupied West Bank.

A BBC team witnessed one of several attacks in farmland near the Palestinian village of Abu Falah. A local official said the attacks had injured 12 Palestinians, including four dual Palestinian American citizens. A foreign journalist was also among those hurt.

Driving into the area early in the morning, we came across the first signs of the violence : a stream of cars carrying wounded Palestinian olive farmers racing out along the narrow stony track, piled high with olive picking equipment, as smoke rose from several fires nearby.

The bloodied face of Majdi Fheed peered out from the backseat of one car.

"We were getting our olive trees and almost 15 Jewish guys … started attacking us with guns, with rocks, with special weapons. They hit me on my head [and] my neck – look, I am bleeding!"

Yaser AlKam, a council member from the neighbouring village of Turmus Aya told me Majdi - an American citizen - was attacked by settlers with nail-studded sticks, and needed treatment for deep wounds on his head. His elderly mother was also injured.

Another man ferrying the injured to hospital told us that settlers had attacked them with sticks while they harvested their olives, and had burned three cars – including one of his own.

"As soon as we got to the land and put our things on the ground, they started to come, so we ran away" said a woman next to him.

Asked about the violence, a US State Department spokesperson said they were aware of the reports.

"We condemn criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and call for investigations, arrests, and convictions, of those responsible," the spokesperson said.

Watching the vehicles stream past her, 73-year-old Imm Khaldoun told me emphatically that, no matter what happened, she would always return to her land. "This is my land. It's my right [to be here]" she told me.

The UN says the past two weeks have already seen more attacks by violent Israeli settlers than during the entire harvest season last year.

Olive picking in the West Bank is now a test of speed, with trees rapidly stripped of fruit as soon as the sun rises, before violent Israeli settlers attack.

In another olive orchard nearby, we watched as dozens of farmers used power-tools to strip the trees as fast as they could – one eye on the ridge above us, where a group of settlers at a new illegal outpost had already gathered, and were watching the olive harvest below.

Standing on ladders, the Palestinian farmers worked quickly, sending streams of olives onto the plastic sheets laid out under the trees. Three villages had come together to harvest these olives, the landowner Amin Khalil, told me, as a form of protection against attack. He said his land was now surrounded by seven Jewish settlements and outposts.

All Israeli settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts – small encampments on hilltops – are illegal under Israeli law as well, but many still receive state support.

"This is a hotspot – there are seven settlements around here," Amin Khalil told me. "This year, all the people came together because when there are just a few people working alone at the edge of the village, the settlers attack. So all the families are working together today."

But the tactic doesn't work today. As we watch, dozens of settlers, all dressed in black, begin moving down the hill towards us, setting fire to several groups of olive trees.

There are shouts of panic from the Palestinian farmers, yelling for children to get out of the field. Some begin swiftly wrapping up the olives to leave.

But with large numbers of people on both sides, the confrontation stalls into an uneasy stalemate. We see settlers with slingshots hurl stones towards us, and young Palestinian men running to throw stones in return.

As Israeli forces arrive, the standoff explodes into action. Settlers begin running down towards us as the farmers swiftly retreat. Some Palestinians set off fireworks to try and push the settlers back.

American journalist Heidi Levine of the Washington Post was injured in the attack. She described how dozens of settlers ambushed her as she was reporting at the scene.

"I got jumped," she said. "I was on the ground and they were kicking me and I was trying to hold onto my camera and my bag. I had my helmet and flak jacket on which protected me. They made me stand up and they kicked me again, and this went on for at least 10 minutes."

In a statement, Washington Post executive editor Matt Murray said Levine had been clearly identifiable as a journalist.

"We are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities," he said.

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said personnel had been despatched to the area "following a report of a violent confrontation". It said a female journalist had been injured during the confrontation. And that "all circumstances" surrounding the incident would be examined.

As the farmers retreated, the sound of live ammunition cracked across the fields. It was unclear if settlers or Israeli forces were firing.

Minutes later, Israeli forces began firing tear gas into the Palestinian fields to end the confrontation – a well-worn Israeli pattern of managing these conflicts.

The UN says settler attacks on the olive harvest this year have so far killed one Palestinian and injured more than 120 others across the West Bank.

Illegal Jewish outposts have mushroomed here over the past few years, clustering in closer around Palestinian olive groves.

What we witnessed was part of a pattern being repeated day after day, as settler outposts here increase.

The yearly olive harvest has become a litmus test of how the policies of Israel's fiercely pro-settlement government are affecting Palestinians here, by presiding over growing violence by extremist settlers, and fuelling Jewish claims to the land.

articles.title: 6,000 cops, 2 notices, Dipke among 150 detained: How unrest unfolded during CP 'Tiranga march'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The day that began with Delhi Police reaching Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke’s residence, escalated into detentions at
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The day that began with Delhi Police reaching Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke’s residence, escalated into detentions at Connaught Place and Mandi House, and saw hundreds of protesters turn up with the Tricolour amid a heavy security deployment.By Friday evening, around 150 people had been detained during the planned ‘Lehra Do Tiranga’ march and parallel demonstrations in central Delhi.The protests had been called against the detention of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were sent to five days of judicial custody after allegedly entering Jantar Mantar without authorisation.As Dipke urged people to wave the national flag at Connaught Place, student and Left organisations planned a separate demonstration near Mandi House, demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.Police reach Dipke’s residence before the marchMore than 20 Delhi Police personnel visited Dipke’s residence in Jhandewalan earlier on Friday and served him a notice directing him to refrain from any action that could prejudice the rights of citizens, traders, commuters, patients and others.Dipke had called for people to gather at Central Park in Connaught Place at 5pm with the Tricolour.In a video posted on X, he said the march would demonstrate that waving the national flag was not a crime. He had also appealed to people in other cities to organise parallel flag marches.Police subsequently detained Dipke preventively while he was on his way to Connaught Place. He was taken to Jafarpur Kalan police station, police sources said.According to news agency ANI, an officer told Dipke that he was being detained under preventive measures, citing Section 163 restrictions in Connaught Place.Police had also served him a separate notice concerning an earlier undertaking to maintain public peace.Security tightened around Connaught PlaceAhead of the planned march, police cordoned off Central Park, forming a human chain along its metal railings. Rapid Action Force personnel were deployed inside the park, while a tear gas vehicle and a Vajra vehicle were stationed outside.Police personnel were also deployed along Connaught Place’s inner and outer circles to regulate traffic. Authorities cited the lack of official permission, restrictions on public gatherings at Central Park and prohibitory orders in force in the area.The security arrangements came a day after the New Delhi Municipal Council announced that Central Park would remain closed on October 16 and 17 for administrative reasons.Protesters gather, police begin detentionsDespite the restrictions, protesters reached Connaught Place carrying the Tricolour and raising slogans. Police began detaining demonstrators, saying those attempting to disrupt law and order would be taken into custody.By the evening, around 150 people had been detained, police said. A senior officer said the situation remained peaceful and that the priority was to maintain law and order and ensure smooth traffic movement.Police also allowed marches by different groups raising various slogans, even as they continued to remove protesters from restricted areas. The detentions led to jostling among crowds, camera crews and security personnel.AISA chief Neha Bora detained at Mandi HouseMeanwhile, a parallel protest took shape near Mandi House, where members of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) and Left organisations had gathered to demand Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.AISA chief Neha Bora was preventively detained while on her way to join the demonstration. The protesters raised concerns over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the functioning of the Election Commission of India.Hundreds of people, including CJP members and student activists, gathered at Connaught Place and Mandi House for a series of flash protests. Some waved the national flag as police maintained a heavy presence at both locations.More than 6,000 personnel deployedDelhi Police and Central Armed Police Forces deployed more than 6,000 personnel across the capital ahead of the demonstrations.Delhi police commissioner Anurag Kumar visited the DCP New Delhi office at Parliament Street police station to review security arrangements.The commissioner also visited the South Campus and Satya Niketan areas with senior officers to review law and order and student safety.The team interacted with students, particularly women living in paying guest accommodations and hostels, and directed local police to strengthen patrolling and visible security measures.The protests came amid CJP and Opposition parties’ ongoing agitation against alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.They also followed the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue, with Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground identified as alternative locations for demonstrations, subject to permission.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: California wildfires spread amid strong winds; over 150,000 customers without power
articles.summary: Several wildfires were burning across Southern California on Friday as hot, dry and windy weather heightened fire danger, prompting evacuations and
articles.body: Several wildfires were burning across Southern California on Friday as hot, dry and windy weather heightened fire danger, prompting evacuations and leaving more than 150,000 electricity customers across California without power.A fast-moving blaze in Malibu, a coastal community west of Los Angeles, triggered evacuation orders and warnings across a large part of the Santa Monica Mountains. Thick black smoke billowing over the hills was visible on nearby cameras and from locations several miles away.Wind gusts of up to 30 mph (48 kph) were recorded early Friday, with stronger winds expected later, the National Weather Service said, according to the Associated Press. Falling humidity levels were adding to the dangerous fire conditions.“This will favour a critical fire weather threat,” the weather service warned early Friday.More than 285 firefighters battled the Bryson Fire overnight as it spread across approximately 200 acres (81 hectares). The blaze threatened a juvenile detention and rehabilitation facility in Los Angeles County, which was evacuated on Thursday night. Fire officials were expected to provide an update on Friday morning.Fire crews were also working to contain two other blazes that broke out on Thursday afternoon, prompting evacuation orders in Azusa, north of Los Angeles, and at Camp Pendleton, near San Diego.More than 150,000 customers across Northern, Central and Southern California were without electricity as of Friday, according to utilities have increasingly resorted to precautionary power shutdowns during dry and windy weather, as electrical equipment has been linked to some of the state's most destructive wildfires.The dangerous weather conditions were expected to persist through Saturday.Santa Ana winds heighten fire dangerLos Angeles Mayor Karen Bass, who faced criticism over the city's handling of the deadly wildfires in January 2025, directed the fire department to pre-position personnel and equipment ahead of the expected winds. The department also sought assistance from the state's Office of Emergency Services.Rose Schoenfeld, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, said elevated fire danger extended across a wide area and urged communities throughout Southern California to remain vigilant.Dry, warm and gusty northeasterly winds, known as Santa Ana winds, were forecast to blow from inland areas towards the coast and offshore. The strongest winds were expected through Friday afternoon.Winds of 20 to 40 mph (32 to 64 kph), with gusts reaching 50 to 70 mph (80 to 113 kph), were forecast in the San Gabriel Mountains in Los Angeles County and the Santa Susana Mountains, which lie largely in Ventura County, Schoenfeld said.Brief periods of critical fire weather conditions were also expected in parts of the Santa Lucia Mountains in San Luis Obispo County.A wind-driven fire in Azusa scorched more than 40 acres (16 hectares) on Thursday, briefly prompting evacuation orders for a neighbourhood in the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains. Firefighters had halted its spread by mid-afternoon.Further south, a blaze at Camp Pendleton threatened buildings. Military officials said evacuation orders were issued for the base's Las Flores area before being lifted by Thursday evening.Power shutdowns affect Northern CaliforniaIn Northern California, communities in the Sierra Nevada and surrounding foothills began experiencing strong winds, high temperatures and low humidity on Wednesday night.The National Weather Service issued a red flag warning for parts of Central and Northern California through Friday morning, cautioning that any fires that broke out could spread rapidly. Such warnings are issued when weather conditions significantly increase the risk of wildfires.Pacific Gas and Electric Company said power interruptions affecting customers from the Central Coast to the northern reaches of the Sierra Nevada could continue until Saturday afternoon.Wildfire risks persist through the weekendIn Southern California, a red flag warning covering mountainous areas of Ventura and Los Angeles counties remained in effect through Friday night. Hot and windy conditions were expected to continue over the weekend.The latest fires have renewed concerns following the devastating wildfires that struck the Los Angeles area in January 2025.The Palisades Fire, driven by Santa Ana winds, swept through a hillside neighbourhood in Los Angeles, killing 12 people and destroying homes with ocean views. Authorities determined that the blaze was a carryover from an earlier fire that they alleged had been deliberately started by a 29-year-old man.A separate fire in Altadena, also in Los Angeles County, killed 19 people and destroyed more than 9,400 homes and businesses. Officials attributed the blaze to sparks from an idle transmission tower owned by Southern California Edison.Schoenfeld said the forecast Santa Ana winds were not expected to be as powerful as those during the January 2025 fires, when gusts reached 60 to 100 mph (96 to 160 kph).You use AI every day. articles.title: Reform councillor Alan Feeney quits over offensive comments
articles.summary: Alan Feeney was captured on undercover filming calling Asian homeowners "parasites".
articles.body:
Warning: This report contains racist and offensive language.

A Reform UK councillor filmed calling Asian homeowners "parasites" has resigned from two councils and apologised for his comments.

Alan Feeney, who has since stepped down from the party, was heard making the remarks during undercover filming for an ITV News investigation in the run up to council elections in May.

Feeney said he had resigned every post he held on Solihull Council and Birmingham City Council, adding that his remarks "were wrong, offensive and completely unacceptable".

He has also been suspended from his job with the prison service, with the Ministry of Justice [MoJ] describing the comments captured during the documentary as "despicable".

In July, his register of interests with Solihull council recorded he was employed as a custodial manager, a position described on the HM Prison and Probation Service website as "the most senior uniformed officers in a prison".

Feeney was one of several Reform members featured in the ITV investigation, which was gathered over the course of a year.

In it, while campaigning in the run-up to May's elections, Feeney described an area as "infested" with Asian families and called them "absolute parasites".

He was also recorded saying no more than 1% of the UK population should be non-white.

Speaking to the BBC's Today programme on Friday , Reform MP Robert Jenrick said he "didn't like what I heard in the documentary" but argued that the party had acted quickly, removing or suspending those in the undercover film.

He added that all parties had "bad apples" and denied it was any more of a problem in Reform than other parties.

On Thursday, the party told the BBC that Feeney had "mutually agreed" to resign from the party.

Writing on Facebook on Friday, Feeney said he wanted "to offer my sincere and unreserved apologies for the comments I made in the recording that has recently come to light".

He added the comments did "not reflect my true beliefs or opinions, particularly of the communities mentioned in the report".

These were communities he had "supported countless times" over many years, he added.

He stated his true self was reflected in more than a decade of public service, but achievements "cannot reduce the impact of what has been said".

Feeney, who defected from the Conservative Party to Reform last year, was elected to the Shard End ward on Birmingham City Council in May.

A spokesperson for Reform Solihull said Feeney was briefly with the party, but spent the majority of his time as a Conservative councillor, and did not reflect "the views of the group".

The MoJ has stated the comments featured in the documentary would be investigated and action taken in line with its policy.

articles.body: A new $55 million medical facility in South Carolina includes a special outdoor retreat built with a $100,000 donation from country music star Dolly Parton. The gift also honours her family's roots in the local area. The new Union Medical Center, part of the Spartanburg Regional Healthcare System, marked its opening with a ribbon-cutting ceremony. The hospital was built on a 48-acre site along Furman L. Fendley Highway. One of its main features is an outdoor healing garden. It offers a peaceful, open-air space for patients recovering from illness, visiting families and hospital staff. Parton's donation went directly to the facility's Patient Enhancement Project, which paid for the garden's construction and landscaping. The space gives people a quiet place to rest away from hospital wards and treatment rooms.Deep family roots in Union CountyAlthough Parton is widely linked to the Great Smoky Mountains of East Tennessee, her family history is closely tied to Union County, South Carolina. Her mother, Avie Lee Owens Parton, was born in the nearby town of Lockhart on 5 October 1923. Local history records show that Avie Lee was the daughter of a local preacher. Parton has often described her mother as her first musical influence and a source of emotional support. According to local television station WLTX, these family ties led the singer and philanthropist to support the regional healthcare project. The donation was arranged through the Spartanburg Regional Foundation, which led the private fundraising effort to help pay for the new medical centre.Specialized space for patient recoveryThe healing garden was designed to extend the hospital's care spaces into the outdoors. It includes paved paths, outdoor seating, green spaces and quiet areas. These features are intended to help reduce stress for families dealing with medical emergencies and other health challenges. Medical staff and healthcare leaders at Spartanburg Regional Healthcare System highlighted the role of natural spaces in helping patients recover. According to the 2024 Spartanburg Regional Foundation Impact Report, the hospital was designed to offer a complete approach to healthcare. It brings modern emergency care and doctors' offices together under one roof, while also providing easy access to green spaces. The report noted that Parton was joined by other donors, including local community leader Barbara Rippy and J. Carlisle Oxner III. They provided significant financial support to improve the environment for patients at the new centre. During the hospital's opening events, Parton sent a personal message to hospital leaders and the Union community. She expressed her support for the staff and the patients who will use the new space.Broader philanthropic footprintThe $100,000 donation to Union Medical Center is part of Parton's wider record of charitable work in healthcare, education and disaster relief. According to official information on her philanthropy website, much of her charitable work is carried out through the Dollywood Foundation, which was established in 1988. The foundation runs the Imagination Library, a book-gifting programme that has sent more than 200 million free books to children from birth to age five. The programme operates across the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the Republic of Ireland. Parton has also made major donations to medical institutions over several decades. In 2020, she donated $1 million to Vanderbilt University Medical Centre in Nashville, Tennessee. The money helped support early research and development of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine. She also funded the Hannah Dennison Center at East Tennessee Children's Hospital, named in honour of her niece, and supported research programmes focused on childhood cancer. The healing garden at Union Medical Center provides a lasting tribute to Parton's mother and her family's history in South Carolina.
