articles.title: Tiger attack victim's medical records may have been breached
articles.summary: William Chapman, 24, was mauled to death at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, near Doncaster, on Saturday.
articles.body:
Medical records belonging to a man killed by a tiger at Yorkshire Wildlife Park may have been accessed "without a legitimate reason" by staff at Yorkshire Ambulance Service, a spokesperson has said.

William Chapman, 24, was mauled to death at the park near Doncaster on Saturday.

In a statement, the trust said following Chapman's death it had identified two possible incidents of staff "accessing or attempting to access incident/medical information" about the case.

It said an investigation had been launched "to establish the full circumstances surrounding these potential breaches".

Chapman died as a result of "multiple traumatic injuries and animal interaction" after entering the tiger's enclosure at the park, an inquest into his death heard on Thursday.

In a statement, a spokesperson for Yorkshire Ambulance Service NHS Trust said Chapman's family was aware of the potential breach and offered their condolences to his relatives.

They said: "We believe there may have been two instances involving two members of staff accessing or attempting to access incident/medical information following this incident without a legitimate reason to do so.

"We take the confidentiality and security of patient information extremely seriously and have robust systems in place to protect information, and this concern has been identified as a result of our proactive audits.

"The trust has commenced an investigation to establish the full circumstances surrounding these potential breaches and the actions of these individuals.

"We have also reported this matter to the Information Commissioner's Office and we will continue to keep William's family informed as our investigation progresses."

An inquest at Doncaster Coroner's Court on Thursday heard that Chapman had died of "multiple traumatic injuries" .

Chapman had attended the park at about 13:30 BST on Saturday, climbed over two fences and entered the tiger enclosure.

After the attack, park staff secured the tiger and paramedics attended, who confirmed Chapman's death at the scene, the inquest was told.

Senior coroner Nicola Mundy said Chapman had a history of mental illness, a diagnosis of schizophrenia and had suffered previous bouts of psychosis.

The inquest heard that the 24-year-old was under adult mental health services in Doncaster, but was "highly functioning and independent with no care requirements".

The self-employed online trader was born in Chichester, West Sussex, and lived in Doncaster at the time of his death.

A government has given a tourism body £500,000 to attract more visitors in 2027.

Ministers have approved the top-up grant for Visit Jersey for advertising and campaigns to attract tourists.

The Government of Jersey said the hospitality sector had seen an "improved season" in 2026 and it was "vital that this upward trend continues to help stabilise the sector, which had faced rising cost pressures and relatively low visitor numbers in recent years".

It said the investment supported its objective to grow the visitor economy by increasing overnight leisure visits and total visitor spend.

It said that by issuing the top-up grant now, the tourism board would be able to act to secure the advertising space and marketing campaigns required to boost visitor numbers in 2027.

articles.title: Loans granted while Burnham was mayor investigated by councillors
articles.summary: A senior councillor says concerns have been raised about the transparency of the process to approve the loans.
articles.body:
Loans made to property companies - including three controlled by Manchester City's Abu Dhabi owner - while Andy Burnham was Greater Manchester mayor are being investigated by councillors.

About 50 developers have been lent more than £1bn between them from a fund managed by the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) since 2015.

John Leech, the chairman of the GMCA's Overview and Scrutiny Committee, told the BBC concerns had been raised about the transparency of the process to approve the loans.

"We just want to be clear that there is a transparent rather than an opaque process," said Leech, who is the Liberal Democrat opposition leader on Manchester City Council.

He said the approval process had been criticised as "very opaque in the past and that it's not necessarily been clearly understood why X was successful and Y wasn't".

A GMCA spokesperson said it was supporting the committee with its enquiries.

The money came from the Greater Manchester Housing Investment Loan Fund (GMHILF).

The fund was set up in 2015 with an initial £300m of government investment to help developers build new homes across Greater Manchester.

Three property companies ultimately controlled by Manchester City owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan were granted loans worth about £55m in total.

The decisions to approve these loans were taken in 2017, in two meetings which were both chaired by Andy Burnham when he was mayor of Greater Manchester.

The decisions to grant loans from the fund were taken publicly by all members of the GMCA, not the mayor alone.

One of Manchester's leading property developers, Renaker, has received the majority of the £1bn lent out from the fund.

Renaker has been involved in a long-running legal battle over £140m worth of loans made to the developer through the GMCA's fund.

A rival developer, Aubrey Weis, claims the the loans were unfair subsidies.

In June, the Court of Appeal found there had been "no error of law" in the GMCA's decision to provide the loans but Weis is appealing the decision.

The Overview & Scrutiny Committee, which reviews the activities of the mayor and the GMCA, agreed to launch an inquiry into the loans earlier this year and Leech is now taking that work forward, after being elected chairman recently.

Leech, a former Lib Dem MP in Manchester, said he felt the fund was intended to be for property companies struggling to access financing.

In 2015, when the loan scheme was launched, Bill Enevoldson, the GMCA's chief investment officer, said : "It is not designed to finance unviable projects but can unlock currently unfundable ones."

An evaluation of the fund from 2025 said it was designed to provide loans for "projects which might otherwise struggle to secure financing".

Leech said it was "not unreasonable" to ask why seemingly successful businesses needed to borrow public money through this loan scheme.

"In the case of Abu Dhabi, you would imagine that they wouldn't have any problem accessing funds from elsewhere as well," Leech said.

"And so the process clearly does seem to be out of kilter with what the original stated aims were back in 2015."

Leech said the committee had asked GMCA officers to produce a report about the use of these funds.

He said the committee will ask officers questions about the fund at a private meeting, before potentially making recommendations to the Greater Manchester mayor.

The committee does not have the power to sanction the mayor but it can investigate, require answers, expose problems and challenge decisions.

The committee could call forward witnesses, such as current Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig, to give evidence as part of the inquiry.

Conservative shadow sports minister Louie French said Burnham had "serious questions to answer" about the loans.

French said "taxpayers deserve transparency over how this money was awarded".

In a statement, the GMCA said the funding for the loans had been lent "at commercial rates" and had delivered "11,000 new homes and regenerating brownfield land across the city region".

The GMCA said "not a single viable scheme was ever turned down".

A GMCA spokesperson added: "The fund is open to all developers, with lending criteria based on parameters set by the government and developed with external financial experts to reflect due diligence standards in the private sector.

"Every penny loaned from the fund is being fully repaid, delivering billions of pounds worth of development at no cost to the taxpayer."

In 2014, Manchester City Council and Abu Dhabi United Group, which owns Manchester City FC, formed a joint venture called Manchester Life.

Abu Dhabi United Group and Manchester Life were involved in three property developments that were partially financed through the GMCA's loan fund.

A Manchester Life spokesperson said: "It is standard for property development to be funded through a combination of investor equity and borrowing.

"All three sites had previously been derelict. The loans were provided on commercial terms and have been repaid in full, including interest."

The BBC asked Renaker for comment but it did not respond before publication.

Julia Hatmaker, the editor of the Place North West property news website, said viability was "always a struggle" in the development world.

She said the GMCA's loan scheme had been successful in building more homes in the city and generating a return on that investment.

But she said it's a "good time for the combined authority to re-evaluate what kind of project it wants to support with similar loan programmes and whether it wants to put stricter rules in place as to what developments can benefit from them".

articles.title: Texas woman sues taco chain after finding a cow’s tooth in her to-go order
articles.summary: ‘Her reaction was disgust. ‘What is this?’ the woman’s lawyer said
articles.body:
A Texas woman is suing a taco chain after finding a cow's tooth in her to-go order, according to reports.

​Nohemi Castillo, who filed her lawsuit on October 13, says that she had purchased a Democrat taco from Torchy's Tacos in Austin , only to discover the tooth inside. Upon making the discovery, she was left "grossed out and sickened" and eventually decided to visit a doctor that same evening, according to her lawsuit, which was reviewed by Fox 7 .

​The doctor prescribed Castillo prescription medication on June 9, the day she discovered the tooth. She is now seeking $250,000, her lawsuit states.

​Scott Vasquez, Castillo's lawyer, told KVUE that his client was horrified to see the tooth in her meal.

​"Her reaction was disgust. 'What is this?'" he revealed. "Looking at it, she thought it was a tooth."

​A picture of the tooth was included with Castillo's lawsuit. In the image, the tooth, slicked in a brown liquid, can be seen next to what appears to be the remains of the woman's Democrat taco .

​A Democrat taco contains beef barbacoa with avocado, cotija cheese, cilantro, diced onions and tomatillo salsa, according to the Torchy's Tacos website . The item was given its name during a promotion by the company, during which it also offered Republican and Independent tacos.

​When Vasquez informed Torchy's Tacos about Castillo discovering the tooth in her Democrat taco, a manager and lawyer tried to shift the blame for the incident, he told KVUE.

​"I thought they'd want to take care of this immediately, and apparently not," he jabbed. "They just felt, in my view: 'Let's blame someone else.'"

​In her lawsuit, Castillo has accused Torchy's Tacos of negligence and of breach of implied warranties, as well as violations of the Deceptive Trade Practices Act and the Food Safety Modernization Act, Fox 7 reports.

​The fast food chain told the outlet that it is aware of the incident and confirmed that the object found in Castillo's meal was, in fact, a cow tooth.

​"We source the highest quality food available, which means our barbacoa comes from natural beef cheek that we source from a supplier," a spokesperson said in a statement. "Upon receiving the guest complaint, we conducted a thorough review and identified the item as a cow tooth."

​"This can occasionally happen when processing the meat, though it is quite rare," the spokesperson added. "We have partnered with our supplier to reinforce their internal procedures to prevent this from happening in the future."

​However, Vasquez says that the tooth should not have made it all the way through the production process into someone's meal .

​"Someone should have caught it somewhere throughout the process," he told KVUE. "Should not have even made it to the packaging or the packaged goods that they had."

​Vasquez added, "It could choke somebody. It really could."

The Independent has contacted Torchy's Tacos for comment.

articles.title: A US Army soldier was off duty near Fort Bragg when he heard gunshots, found a wounded man and used a tourniquet, pressure dressing and chest seal; two weeks later, he received the Army Commendation Medal
articles.summary: An off-duty US Army soldier stepped in to help a gunshot victim near Fort Bragg after hearing gunfire near his home in North Carolina.
articles.body: An off-duty US Army soldier stepped in to help a gunshot victim near Fort Bragg after hearing gunfire near his home in North Carolina. Private First Class Stephen Bradley received the Army Commendation Medal for quickly giving medical care to the injured civilian until emergency services arrived. Brigadier General Raphael S. Heflin, commanding general of the 3rd Corps Sustainment Command, presented the award during a ceremony. Bradley, who is from Spanish Town, Jamaica, serves as a motor transport operator with the 126th Composite Truck Company, 264th Combat Sustainment Support Battalion, 3rd Corps Sustainment Command. He was off duty at his home in Spring Lake, just outside Fort Bragg, when the shooting happened.Response to off-post gunfireAfter hearing several gunshots outside his home, Bradley went outside to see what had happened. He found a civilian with multiple gunshot wounds who needed immediate medical help. "I heard several shots and immediately went out to see what happened," Bradley said in an official report published by the United States Army. "When I saw someone was wounded, my training immediately took over. All that mattered was getting to him and keeping him stable." Bradley approached an off-duty police officer who was already at the scene. He identified himself as a soldier trained in military combat lifesaver skills. He then collected his emergency medical kit and began treating the victim.Emergency treatment at the sceneBradley worked directly on the injured man. He placed a tourniquet on the man's arm to stop heavy bleeding. He also used a pressure dressing and a chest seal to help stabilize other injuries. Local first responders confirmed that Bradley's quick use of advanced first aid was vital in keeping the patient alive until paramedics arrived and took him to a hospital. According to the US Army report, local civilian law enforcement agencies are leading the ongoing criminal investigation into the shooting.Military recognition and training impactDuring the award ceremony, Heflin praised Bradley for taking action. He also highlighted how standard military medical training can be useful in emergencies outside the military. "This is a clear testament to why combat lifesaver qualification is so vital across our entire formation," Heflin said during the ceremony. "When seconds count, that training saves lives, whether in combat or right here in our local communities. Pfc. Bradley is exactly the kind of Soldier you want standing beside you as your battle buddy, because when an emergency happened, he didn't hesitate to act." The Combat Lifesaver course is a standard training programme for military personnel who are not medical professionals. It teaches them how to provide immediate treatment for serious injuries under pressure. The training covers ways to control severe bleeding, manage airways and treat chest wounds. articles.title: Russia building 'security zone' in Ukraine that won't be part of future peace talks: Putin
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday said Moscow is building a buffer “security zone” inside Ukraine which won’t be a part of any future peace
articles.body: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday said Moscow is building a buffer “security zone” inside Ukraine which won’t be a part of any future peace negotiations, describing the move as necessary to protect Russia’s border regions.Putin made the remarks during a visit to a command post of Russia’s joint military task force. He linked the operation to Ukraine’s incursion into Russia’s western Kursk region in 2024-25, saying Russian forces had been directed to push Ukrainian troops out of Russian territory and extend the operation into neighbouring Ukrainian territory.“The Russian armed forces were tasked not only with expelling the enemy from our land but also with establishing a security zone in the adjacent territory. This task is being carried out successfully,” he said in televised comments.“Our goal is to ensure the absolute security of Russia’s border regions for the future, and we do not plan to make this a subject for potential peace negotiations with Ukraine.”Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the proposed security zone would cover a stretch of 660 km (410 miles), with Russian forces controlling 70 per cent of the area.Putin was also quoted by the Kremlin as saying that Russia still needed to capture more of Ukraine’s Donetsk region. Reuters reported.The latest remarks follow the Kremlin’s announcement in July that Russia was working to establish a buffer zone along the border.“Given the aggressive nature of the Kyiv regime, in order to ensure the safety of our citizens, we will have to create a security zone, or buffer zone,” Peskov had told a Russian journalist, according to Anadolu Agency.Peskov said the initiative was progressing steadily and pointed to advances made by Russian troops.“It is being created, and it is being created systematically,” he said in remarks carried by Russian media outlets, including state news agency Tass, arguing that “significant results” had been achieved in terms of Russian troop advances.He also maintained that Moscow would continue the operation until the zone reached the scale it considered necessary for its security.The spokesperson had remarked that no one should doubt that the “buffer zone” would be created “to the extent necessary to ensure our security.”You use AI every day. articles.summary: Bill Gates’ ex-wife Melinda French Gates and their daughters Jennifer Gates Nassar and Phoebe Gates have joined a group of philanthropists as founding
articles.body: Bill Gates’ ex-wife Melinda French Gates and their daughters Jennifer Gates Nassar and Phoebe Gates have joined a group of philanthropists as founding supporters of the Women’s Health Co-Lab. It is a collaborative fund which aims at mobilising $100 million to improve the health and wellbeing of women and girls globally. According to a report by Luxury Launches, the initiative was launched by ICONIQ Impact in partnership with Co-Impact at the 2025 Forbes Impact Summit. The initiative is focused on addressing some of the most pressing challenges facing women globally, including maternal health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and gender-based violence. The programme has already secured more than $70 million in commitments from founding donors, including the Gates family members and 14 other philanthropists.Bill Gates’ daughter Phoebe Gates highlights ongoing challenges for womenSpeaking about the initiative, Phoebe Gates, co-founder and co-CEO of Phia, stressed that significant barriers to women's health and safety remain despite years of advocacy."It is unacceptable that in 2025, women are still fighting the same battles for health and safety," she said. "Yet these 22 organizations give us reason to believe change is possible. They are pushing forward, protecting reproductive freedom, confronting violence, and demanding better care for mothers."According to the organisers, the fund will support 22 organisations selected from a pool of more than 400 applicants. These groups will receive unrestricted funding over the next three years to strengthen healthcare access, legal protections, information networks and support systems for women and girls.22 grantees chosen from over 400The Co-Lab supports 22 organizations working on the root causes of health inequity for women and girls, picked from a pool of more than 400. Each will receive unrestricted funding over three years. The aim is to strengthen the systems that determine whether women get care, information, legal protection or personal autonomy. The funding targets issues including preventable deaths during pregnancy, gender-based violence and barriers to family planning services.Melinda French Gates doubles down on women's healthThe latest commitment builds on Melinda French Gates' growing focus on women's health philanthropy through her investment and incubation company, Pivotal Ventures. According to reports, she announced a separate $215 million commitment to women's health in 2026, bringing her total funding for the cause over two years to more than $600 million.The Women’s Health Co-Lab has been established around the belief that women and girls, regardless of where they live, should have access to healthcare, safety and bodily autonomy. Organisers say millions of women around the world continue to face preventable maternal deaths, barriers to family planning services and violence that threaten their wellbeing.Daughters follow mother's philanthropic pathThe initiative also highlights how the next generation of the Gates family is becoming increasingly involved in philanthropy. Jennifer Gates Nassar, a paediatric resident, has worked alongside her mother on women's healthcare issues, while Phoebe Gates has publicly advocated for reproductive rights and broader women's health issues.The funding is expected to support projects ranging from maternal healthcare and contraception access to programmes aimed at preventing gender-based violence. Among the organisations selected for support are Every Mother Counts, Americans for Contraception, Girl Effect, Serenas and Ujamaa Africa.Fund still seeking additional supportWhile the initiative has already mobilised more than $70 million, organisers are continuing efforts to reach the $100 million target. The founders say additional philanthropic support will help expand programmes designed to improve health outcomes and increase opportunities for women and girls across multiple countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: Sean 'Diddy' Combs moves from New Jersey prison to facility in Pennsylvania
articles.summary: The decision to move the rap mogul while he is serving out his 50-month sentence was made with 'safety and security in mind'.
articles.body:
Sean "Diddy" Combs has been transferred from a New Jersey correctional facility to a prison in Pennsylvania, the US Federal Bureau of Prisons says.

The rap mogul was moved to FCI Allenwood Low on Friday, a prison official said, but declined to discuss why he was moved, citing privacy, safety, and security reasons.

"His transfer from one low-security facility to another is an important distinction," Combs' spokesman told the BBC, adding that the move "is consistent with a decision made with safety and security in mind".

Combs, 56, who was sentenced to 50 months behind bars, has asked an appeals court to release him from prison and overturn his conviction on two prostitution-related crimes.

Combs' spokesman, Juda S Engelmayer, did not comment on an Associated Press report that Combs had been living a "luxury lifestyle" behind bars in New Jersey or on the tabloid reports swirling about his health and treatment in lockup.

Engelmayer said he appreciates that the Federal Bureau of Prisons is "taking the safety and security of Sean and everyone involved seriously" and "we are grateful for the attention being given to his well-being and hope he can continue serving his time without unnecessary disruption".

The Federal Bureau of Prisons declined to comment on the reports.

"For privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any incarcerated individual, including whether a particular individual is the subject of allegations, investigations, or disciplinary sanctions," spokesman Donald Murphy said.

FCI Allenwood Low is a low-security federal correctional institution for male offenders that is about 155 miles (250 km) west of New York City.

The facility houses about 1,044 inmates, according to its website, a significantly smaller population than the one at Combs' previous facility, Fort Dix, of more than 4,200 inmates across two campuses. Allenwood also has medium and maximum security facilities nearby.

What has Sean 'Diddy' Combs been convicted of?

Sean 'Diddy' Combs files appeal asking for immediate prison release

Federal prosecutors in New York have accused Combs of using his money, power, and the threat of violence to coerce women into unwanted sexual encounters.

After a high-profile jury trial in New York last year, two of Combs' ex-girlfriends testified that he abused them and forced them to participate in so-called "freak-offs" with male escorts.

In July 2025, Combs was convicted on two counts of transportation to engage in prostitution. They jury acquitted him of two more serious charges, sex trafficking and racketeering conspiracy, and he was sentenced to more than four years in prison that October.

Later that month, Combs was transferred to the federal correctional institution at Fort Dix in New Jersey, where he had been serving out his sentence until his transfer on Friday.

In April, a US appeals court heard arguments to overturn his prison sentence but has not yet issued a decision.

He is due to be released from prison on 2 March 2028, according to the prison's online records.

articles.title: ‘You don’t have to do this’: Donald Trump tells new press secretary Katie Zacharia she can quit if she wants
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday suggested that new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia reconsider her position, saying she had faced harsh
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Friday suggested that new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia reconsider her position, saying she had faced harsh treatment from the media and that the job might not be right for her.Meanwhile, Zacharia is “transitioning out” of the position, Fox News reported, citing a White House officialSpeaking to reporters, Trump said he had personally advised Zacharia to consider whether she wanted to continue in the role, which she took up less than a week ago. He added that the decision would ultimately be hers.“I said to Katie just two minutes ago, I said, Katie, you know, you don't have to do this if you don't want,” Trump told reporters. “She said, this is a lot tougher. I said, welcome to the world of Trump.”Asked whether he intended to retain her, Trump said he would leave the decision to her.“I'm going to let her make that decision,” he said, adding that he wanted her to be happy.Trump repeatedly defended Zacharia, describing her as a “nice person” and a “great person”, while criticising the media coverage she had received since becoming the administration's chief spokesperson.“She's been treated very badly by the media. Very, very badly. Very unfairly, I think,” he said.Referring to her recent television appearances, Trump said she had faced tough questioning on Fox News programmes, including interviews with Sean Hannity and Fox & Friends.“I don't think they'll ever ease up,” he said, adding that he had advised her to reconsider the position because of the pressure involved.“Honestly, if I were you, I'd reconsider,” Trump said he had told her.He also referred to Zacharia's husband and children, saying she did not need to put herself through the pressure if she did not want to.Scrutiny over legal credentialsZacharia's first days as White House press secretary have been marked by scrutiny over her professional background and her debut press briefing, which lasted around 14 minutes and drew criticism for its brevity and her reliance on notes.She has also faced questions over her use of the terms “lawyer” and “attorney”, after it emerged that she had not passed the bar exam required to practise law in the United States.Trump had described her as an attorney when announcing her appointment. Zacharia, who graduated from Pepperdine University's law school in 2011, has said she worked in international transaction law and that she used the term “lawyer” rather than “attorney” to distinguish her description from that of a licensed legal practitioner.During an interview with Fox News host Sean Hannity on Thursday, Zacharia defended her performance at her first briefing, saying she had little time to prepare between accepting the job and facing reporters.She also said she was being hired as White House press secretary rather than White House counsel.A watchdog group, Campaign for Accountability, had filed a complaint with the California State Bar Association seeking an investigation into whether Zacharia had repeatedly presented herself as qualified to practise law without a licence.The White House has defended her appointment. Communications director Steven Cheung described Zacharia as “uniquely qualified and whip smart to help inform the American people”, according to the BBC.Trump says he wants her to be happyDespite raising doubts about whether Zacharia should remain in the role, Trump said he was not necessarily asking her to leave.“Look, she has suffered over the last few days,” he said. “And I'm not saying, you know, I mean, maybe it's not for her.”When asked what he wanted her to do, Trump replied: “I just want her to be happy.”Zacharia replaced Karoline Leavitt, who left the position in August. Her appointment had been presented as a rapid transition into the role, but the scrutiny over her initial briefing and legal credentials has placed her under pressure during her first week.Trump did not announce a decision on her future, saying instead that Zacharia would have to decide whether she wanted to continue as White House press secretary.You use AI every day. articles.title: SCB razes function halls on 4 acres of defence land
articles.summary: SCB begins demolishing unauthorised function halls on 4 acres of B-3 defence land in Sikh Village, Hyderabad, after a 30-year legal battle and court order.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Secunderabad Cantonment Board (SCB) on Friday began demolishing unauthorised commercial structures on a four-acre parcel of B-3 defence land in Sikh Village, following a legal battle that began in 1996. The property housed KJR Gardens and Viceroy Garden function halls, which were being used for commercial purposes despite the land being earmarked for residential use, according to SCB officials. The demolition began around 5:30 am, with locals initially resisting the action. Police were deployed at the site to prevent any law and order issues.“The board has been actively identifying locations where unauthorised activities are taking place on defence land. While some disputes are still pending in court, we are taking action as and when court orders are pronounced. There are around 120 old grant bungalows spread across 400 acres of defence land, but the board does not maintain an active record of every individual property,” said SCB CEO Arvind Dwivedi.“The board had approached the court in 1996 seeking demolition of the function hall and has pursued the case since then. The court ruled in the board’s favour earlier this week, paving the way for the demolition,” said Ch Uma Shankar, Cantonment engineer.B-3 is a category of Cantonment land that includes properties held under lease or old grant terms. Such land is recorded in the General Land Register (GLR), with the rights of occupants governed by the applicable grant conditions. In the case of old grant properties, the land may vest with the Union govt, while occupants hold specific rights subject to the terms of the grant. The demolition is part of SCB’s efforts to act against alleged unauthorised use of defence land. articles.title: Prayagraj’s oldest Durga Puja barwaris uphold tradition in 2026
articles.summary: Prayagraj Durga Puja 2026: Four oldest barwari committees uphold traditional rituals, cultural programmes and historic community celebrations across the city.
articles.body: Prayagraj: While elaborate gates and theme-based pandals have become a defining feature of Durga Puja in Prayagraj, four century-old Barwaris continue to keep the focus on tradition. Colonelganj, Indian Girls’ (City), Attarsuyia and Lukerganj Barwaris, among the city’s oldest community puja committees, are once again observing the festival in 2026 with rituals and cultural practices rooted in their long histories.The Colonelganj Barwari is celebrating its 174th Durga Puja this year. The committee was formally formed in 1853, when devotees decided to move the worship from individual homes to a community celebration. Its first organised puja was held at the residence of Ram Chandra Banerjee, in the outer verandah of his house near Bhardwaj Ashram. The venue remained there for about two decades before being shifted elsewhere and finally, by the early 1920s, moved to the large plot opposite Anand Bhawan.The president of this oldest barwari of the city, Shankar Chaterjee, said the puja may have been held occasionally earlier, but 1853 marked its beginning as an organised community event. In those days, celebrations included folk songs and Bengali Jatra performances. Even basic requirements such as cotton carpets and utensils were not available on hire, and Motilal Nehru and his family provided the necessary items, he said. Hindi dramatist Bhartendu Harish Chandra also staged a Hindi play during the festival and acted in it himself, Chaterjee added.The Indian Girls’ (City) Barwari, associated with the Chowk area, has a history of more than 142 years. Unlike most locality-based committees, its members are spread across Prayagraj. In its early years, the committee included Bengalis and non-Bengalis, particularly businessmen from Chowk. Its puja remains distinctly traditional, from the priest and bhog to the simple idol that largely retains the same form each year. Its dhuni dance remains another popular attraction.The Attarsuyia Barwari, formed in 1882, is observing its 144th year in 2026. Member Sachin Kesarvani said the committee has traditionally sought to create an attractive celebration with limited resources while supporting local artists. Its relatively compact pandal carries a social theme each year, conveyed through handmade posters and banners.The Bai Ka Bagh Barwari is also marking its centenary in 2026 with a grand Kerala-inspired theme. Its 60-foot-high pandal is being designed as a replica of the iconic Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple in Thiruvananthapuram, with eight doors inspired by the temple’s famed treasury doors. An idol of Lord Vishnu will be installed inside, while six dhak artistes from Kolkata have been invited to add a traditional Bengali touch to the celebrations.The Lukerganj Barwari, meanwhile, reflects the strong Bengali presence in the locality, which was named after British officer Luker. The Barwari, formed as part of the area’s Bengali community, is known not only for Durga Puja and Lakshmi Puja but also for fairs, dramas, dances and other cultural programmes, keeping the festival connected with the city’s cultural heritage.Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news. articles.title: Fill 3,000 vacant faculty posts in varsities, teachers urge govt
articles.summary: Telangana teachers urge govt to fill 3,000 vacant university faculty posts, not just recruit 500; seek regular hires and regularisation of 1,200 contract staff.
articles.body: Hyderabad: With several state universities grappling with a faculty shortage, members of the Telangana Schools and Technical Colleges Employees Association on Friday urged the govt to fill all vacant posts immediately.In a letter to the special chief secretary of education, the association questioned the proposed recruitment of 500 faculty members when around 3,000 posts remain vacant in state universities.“The shortage was adversely affecting the quality of education, academic activities, research and students’ futures. Recruiting only 500 faculty members would leave a substantial number of vacancies unfilled and further aggravate the problems facing higher education,” the letter added.The association also pointed out that many universities depended on contractual faculty members to manage their academic responsibilities. It urged the govt to prioritise the recruitment of qualified, regular faculty members to reduce this dependence.“The govt must review contractual appointments and discontinue those that are no longer required, in accordance with applicable rules and due process, while ensuring that essential academic activities are not disrupted,” said A Santhosh Kumar, president of the association.Meanwhile, contract assistant professors working at various universities have been demanding regularisation of their services and the implementation of UGC 7th Pay Commission pay scales.“About 1,200 contract faculty members have been working in state universities for the past three decades. The govt must first absorb these faculty members before undertaking fresh recruitment. articles.title: Role Women farmer producer companies (WFPCs) can play in redefining gender roles & turning women farmers into agri-entrepreneurs in Indian agriculture
articles.summary: Introduction Women-led Farmer Producer Companies (WFPCs) in India are emerging as powerful vehicles: Recognising women as farmers; Dismantling
articles.body: IntroductionWomen-led Farmer Producer Companies (WFPCs) in India are emerging as powerful vehicles:Recognising women as farmers;Dismantling land-ownership based definitions, and;Turning SHG (Self Help Group) members into agribusiness entrepreneurs, backed by:New laws,Global initiatives, and;SRLM (State Rural Livelihood Mission) support.WFPCs can:Reshape gender roles;Strengthen climate-smart agriculture, and give women:a) Formal ownership;b) Leadership, and;c)Market bargaining power, across agrifood value chains.Farmer Producer Company (FPC)The concept of the Farmer Producer Company in India originated from the recommendations of the Y.K. Alagh Committee in the early 2000s.The FPC framework was introduced in 2002 by incorporating it into the Companies Act, 1956, strengthening it further under the Companies Act, 2013.An FPC is a legal entity, Collectively Owned by Primary Producers, and designed to Collectivise:· Farmers;· Fishers, and;· Village artisans.The primary objective of an FPC is:· To collectivise marginal and small farmers;· Enable them to access markets through product aggregation, and;· Enhance their collective bargaining power.Acting as a Hybrid between Cooperatives and Corporate Companies, this model provides:· Mutual benefits to its members similar to a cooperative, while;· Offering the Corporate competitiveness required for the Agrifood market.Profile of Women Farmers & FPCs in IndiaAround 89.4 percent of farming households in India consist of small and marginal farmers holding less than two hectares of land with Agriculture contributing around 18 per cent to the Nation’s GDP (Gross Domestic Product).As regards the FPCs, a study by the Tata-Cornell Institute and BIRD (Bankers Institute of Rural Development) released in February 2026 reveals that:Out of 44,547 total registered FPCs in India, 6,442 are women-led, or around 15 per cent.Various State Rural Livelihoods Mission (SRLM) Programmes are actively working to graduate women’s Self-Help Groups (SHGs) into formal FPCs.Current Status of Women as FarmersHistorically, women have performed specific, labour-intensive tasks in Indian agriculture, such as:· Seed preservation;· Transplanting;· Weeding, and;· Harvesting.Despite their vital roles, Women:· Are seldom granted decision-making powers, or;· Economic ownership of their produce.However, they have rarely been recognised as farmers,as farmers are defined as land owners.Central Schemes now mandate that:At least 30 percent of funds and benefits be earmarked specifically for women farmers.State level Efforts to Recognise Women as FarmersOver the last two decades, State-led efforts have been made to recognise women as farmers by targeting them as beneficiaries under different Central and State-sponsored Schemes, such as:· MKSP (Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana);· ATMA (Agricultural Technology Management Agency).Maharashtra Women Farmers Empowerment Act, 2026In July 2026, the Maharashtra Assembly passed the Maharashtra Women Farmers Empowerment Act, 2026, becoming the first state to grant activity-based legal recognition to women farmers via:A Woman Farmer Certificate, which decouples Farmer identity from Land ownership.The Act represents a massive socio-economic shift designed to address deeply entrenched gender inequalities regarding access to:1. Land;2. Water;3. Credit, and;4. Other vital natural resources.Women Farmers Producer CompaniesThe history of the Women Farmers Producer Company (WFPC) is rooted in the SHG movements of the 1970s, which have evolved into the Largest Women-led Microfinance Initiative in the world.This movement has been patronised by the government since the 1990s with the perspective of empowering women by:· Overcoming gender stereotypes through financial inclusion;· Providing access to credit;· Promoting leadership skills, and;· Creating platforms to address social issues.EpilogueLimitations & SolutionsOut of the total FPCs promoted nationwide, only 43 per cent to 49 per cent continue to operate effectively, once formal government financial support concludes, highlighting the urgent need to design strategies for the sustainable, independent functioning of WFPCs.Feminisation of agricultureWhile women increasingly play essential roles across agrifood value chains and contribute substantially to the agricultural economy, they are still rarely independent enough to make decisive choices within the household farm economy, such as:· Buying inputs;· Purchasing machinery, or;· Selling farm produce.This limitation stems from embedded structural inequalities that restrict women’s access to:· Information;· Resources;· Opportunities, and;· Strategic decision-making.Because women are culturally left less informed regarding these economic roles, men largely control these decisions, as they are traditionally perceived to be better equipped with:· Market intelligence, and;· Exposure and experience.WFPCs represent an opportunity for a major structural shift, preparing women to actively drive and manage the agricultural sector.WFPCs are powerful tools for women’s empowerment, enabling women to become informed enterprisers:· To take decisive actions, and;· Build a gender-inclusive farm economy.FPCs provide unique opportunities for rural women to be formally recognised as:· Company shareholders, and;· Boards of Directors.Requirement of Community-level actions:Deep-rooted challenges exist at the household and community levels. It is therefore vital to orient both women and men to visualise the benefits of a WFPC.Besides, intensive community engagement is required, specifically targeting men, rather than women.Reshaping deeply ingrained social conditioning is a primary requirement to create a level playing field, where women can confidently occupy decisive, enterprising roles.Policies also must articulate this paradigm shift through time-bound, measurable action plans.Besides, as many women are new to the competitive skills required for contemporary farming, such as:· Precision agriculture;· Climate-compliant practices, and;· Regenerative farming, intensive capacity building is essential, they need to be provided:a) Training in sustainable farm practices;b) Value-chain mechanics;c) Post-harvest management;d) Supply chain negotiations, and;e) Financial literacy, to engage effectively with buyers and bankers.Besides, it is opined, handholding support must be intentionally designed to introduce WFPCs to modern digital market opportunities.The WFPCs open up unprecedented possibilities for the 21st-century agricultural food markets driven by global demand for:· Climate-smart regenerative agriculture;· Safer food systems, and;· Nutrient-dense diets.WFPCs, it is opined, can lead the way by explicitly interlinking these opportunities.Disclaimer: Views expressed above are the author's own.

articles.title: BTC launches Rs 13.9-crore Tipkai–Sapatgram road project
articles.summary: BTC chief Hagrama Mohilary launches Rs 13.91-crore Tipkai–Sapatgram road rebuild and RCC bridge project to boost connectivity in Assam’s BTC region.
articles.body: Dhubri: Bodoland Territorial Council (BTC) chief executive member Hagrama Mohilary has laid the foundation stone for the reconstruction of the Tipkai–Sapatgram road and construction of an RCC bridge at an estimated cost of Rs 13.91 crore.The project will cover the road passing through Belguri and include a four-span reinforced cement concrete bridge, with each span measuring 30 metres. It is intended to improve connectivity and ease the movement of people and vehicles in the surrounding areas.Mohilary laid the foundation stone on Thursday in the presence of Mohammed Antaz Ali, MCLA representing the Guma constituency.According to the project details, the work has been sanctioned for the 2026–27 financial year at an estimated cost of Rs 13.92 crore.Speaking on the occasion, Mohilary said, “Improving road connectivity is one of our priorities for the overall development of the BTC region. The reconstruction of the Tipkai–Sapatgram road, along with the construction of the RCC bridge, will make transportation easier and safer for the people. We are committed to developing better infrastructure to facilitate daily commuting, promote trade and commerce, and improve connectivity in rural areas.”The project is expected to improve access for residents of surrounding villages, facilitate the movement of passengers and goods, and support trade and commercial activities.
